chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Rifah ibn Musa said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), saying: 'I buy a female slave, and she stays with me for months without menstruating, and this is not due to old age.' I said: 'And I showed her to the women, and they said she is not pregnant.' He said: 'Is it permissible for me to have intercourse with her in her private part?' He said: 'Indeed, wind can prevent menstruation without pregnancy, so there is no harm in touching her in the private part.' I said: 'If she is pregnant, what is mine from her if I wish?' He said: 'For you is what is below the private part until she completes four months and ten days of pregnancy.' He said: 'When her pregnancy exceeds four months and ten days, there is no harm in marrying her in the private part.'

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَعَشَرَ أَيَّامٍ: Four months and ten days (a specific gestational period)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on having intercourse with a pregnant female slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the juristic distinction between 'batn' (pregnancy) and 'haidh' (menstruation) in determining the permissibility of sexual relations with a female slave, noting that amenorrhea can be caused by wind or age rather than pregnancy. It establishes a specific gestational threshold of four months and ten days, after which the owner may engage in full vaginal intercourse, reflecting the Shia view on the rights of the master over the concubine during pregnancy. This ruling highlights the practical application of 'wala' (ownership rights) within the framework of marital-like intimacy without full marriage contract requirements.
